theory.title: Exercise 1.3.4: Numeric Comparisons
theory.content:
MENTOR-9 activates two holographic gauge displays showing critical ship systems.

"PROTO-7, sometimes you need to verify values are within safe ranges—temperature below maximum, damage count above threshold. Robot Framework provides dedicated keywords for numeric comparisons."

What are Numeric Comparison Keywords?

Numeric comparison keywords validate relationships between numbers. They're essential for:

  • Threshold validation: Is temperature below danger zone?
  • Range checking: Is value within acceptable limits?
  • Performance metrics: Is response time under maximum?
  • Resource monitoring: Is memory usage above minimum?

Should Be Greater Than

Validates that a number is greater than another:

Should Be Greater Than    ${value}    ${minimum}

Behavior:

  • ✅ If value > minimum → assertion passes
  • ❌ If value ≤ minimum → test fails

Should Be Less Than

Validates that a number is less than another:

Should Be Less Than    ${value}    ${maximum}

Behavior:

  • ✅ If value < maximum → assertion passes
  • ❌ If value ≥ maximum → test fails

Basic Examples

*** Test Cases ***
Temperature Check
    ${temp}            Set Variable    75
    ${max_temp}        Set Variable    100

    Should Be Less Than    ${temp}    ${max_temp}    # ✅ PASSES
    Log                    Temperature within safe limits
*** Test Cases ***
Damage Assessment
    ${damage_count}    Set Variable    5
    ${min_repairs}     Set Variable    3

    Should Be Greater Than    ${damage_count}    ${min_repairs}    # ✅ PASSES
    Log                       Repairs needed!

Complete Comparison Keyword Set

KeywordTest Passes WhenExample
Should Be Greater Than value > minimum 5 > 3 ✅
Should Be Less Than value < maximum 75 < 100 ✅
Should Be Greater Than Or Equal To value ≥ minimum 5 ≥ 5 ✅
Should Be Less Than Or Equal To value ≤ maximum 100 ≤ 100 ✅

Range Validation

Combine comparisons to validate values within a range:

*** Test Cases ***
Safe Operating Range
    ${power_level}     Set Variable    65
    ${min_power}       Set Variable    50
    ${max_power}       Set Variable    100

    # Value must be BETWEEN min and max
    Should Be Greater Than    ${power_level}    ${min_power}     # 65 > 50 ✅
    Should Be Less Than       ${power_level}    ${max_power}     # 65 < 100 ✅
    Log                       Power level within safe range

Number Types

These keywords work with both integers and floating-point numbers:

*** Test Cases ***
Integer and Float Comparisons
    ${int_value}       Set Variable    42
    ${float_value}     Set Variable    3.14

    Should Be Greater Than    ${int_value}      40        # Integers
    Should Be Less Than       ${float_value}    4.0       # Floats
    Should Be Greater Than    ${float_value}    ${int_value}    # Mixed ❌ 3.14 not > 42

Real-World Use Cases

1. System Temperature Monitoring

*** Test Cases ***
Engine Temperature Check
    ${engine_temp}     Set Variable    85
    ${max_safe}        Set Variable    100

    Should Be Less Than    ${engine_temp}    ${max_safe}
    Log                    Engine temperature safe (${engine_temp}°C)

2. Resource Threshold Validation

*** Test Cases ***
Memory Usage Check
    ${used_memory}     Set Variable    4096
    ${min_required}    Set Variable    2048

    Should Be Greater Than    ${used_memory}    ${min_required}
    Log                       Sufficient memory available

3. Performance Metrics

*** Test Cases ***
Response Time Validation
    ${response_ms}     Set Variable    250
    ${max_allowed}     Set Variable    500

    Should Be Less Than    ${response_ms}    ${max_allowed}
    Log                    Response time acceptable (${response_ms}ms)

Error Messages

When comparisons fail, you get clear error messages:

*** Test Cases ***
Failed Comparison
    ${temp}            Set Variable    110
    ${max}             Set Variable    100

    Should Be Less Than    ${temp}    ${max}
    # ❌ ERROR: 110 should be less than 100

Custom Error Messages

Add custom messages for better debugging:

*** Test Cases ***
Clear Error Message
    ${radiation}       Set Variable    55
    ${safe_limit}      Set Variable    50

    Should Be Less Than    ${radiation}    ${safe_limit}
    ...                    msg=Radiation level ${radiation} exceeds safe limit ${safe_limit}!

Failure Output:

AssertionError: Radiation level 55 exceeds safe limit 50!

Numeric vs Boolean Comparisons

AspectNumeric KeywordsShould Be True
Syntax Should Be Less Than ${x} ${y} Should Be True ${x} < ${y}
Readability More explicit, easier to read More compact, Pythonic
Error Messages "42 should be less than 100" "42 < 100 should be true"
When to Use Simple numeric comparisons Complex conditions, multiple checks

Equivalent Comparisons

*** Test Cases ***
Same Validation - Different Approaches
    ${value}           Set Variable    75
    ${max}             Set Variable    100

    # Approach 1: Numeric keyword (clearer)
    Should Be Less Than    ${value}    ${max}

    # Approach 2: Boolean expression (more flexible)
    Should Be True         ${value} < ${max}

Precision with Floats

Floating-point comparisons work but be aware of precision issues:

*** Test Cases ***
Float Precision
    ${pi}              Set Variable    3.14159
    ${approx_pi}       Set Variable    3.14

    Should Be Greater Than    ${pi}    ${approx_pi}    # ✅ 3.14159 > 3.14

    # For precise float comparisons, consider tolerance
    ${difference}      Evaluate    abs(${pi} - 3.14159)
    Should Be Less Than    ${difference}    0.00001

Negative Numbers

Numeric keywords handle negative numbers correctly:

*** Test Cases ***
Negative Number Comparison
    ${temp}            Set Variable    -15
    ${freezing}        Set Variable    0

    Should Be Less Than    ${temp}    ${freezing}    # ✅ -15 < 0

Best Practices

1. Use Descriptive Variable Names

*** Test Cases ***
Descriptive Names
    # ✅ Good: Clear intent
    ${current_temp}    Set Variable    75
    ${max_safe_temp}   Set Variable    100
    Should Be Less Than    ${current_temp}    ${max_safe_temp}

    # ❌ Less clear
    ${a}               Set Variable    75
    ${b}               Set Variable    100
    Should Be Less Than    ${a}    ${b}

2. Add Context with Logging

*** Test Cases ***
Contextual Logging
    ${damage}          Set Variable    7
    ${threshold}       Set Variable    5

    Should Be Greater Than    ${damage}    ${threshold}
    Log                       Damage count (${damage}) exceeds threshold (${threshold}) - repairs required

3. Combine with Custom Messages

*** Test Cases ***
Clear Error Messages
    ${score}           Set Variable    45
    ${passing}         Set Variable    60

    Should Be Greater Than    ${score}    ${passing}
    ...                       msg=Score ${score} below passing grade ${passing}

4. Validate Both Boundaries for Ranges

*** Test Cases ***
Range Validation
    ${value}           Set Variable    75

    # ✅ Good: Validate both min and max
    Should Be Greater Than    ${value}    50
    Should Be Less Than       ${value}    100

    # ✅ Alternative: Use >= and <= if boundaries are inclusive
    Should Be Greater Than Or Equal To    ${value}    50
    Should Be Less Than Or Equal To       ${value}    100

MENTOR-9: "Validate ship systems. Create ${reactor_temp}=85, ${max_temp}=100, verify temp below max. Then create ${hull_damage}=7, ${repair_threshold}=5, verify damage above threshold. Finally, create ${power}=65 and validate it's between 50 and 100. Show me you understand numeric validation."
